results.title: How to Write Data Labeling/Annotation Guidelines
results.content: # How to Write Data Labeling/Annotation Guidelines. Writing data labeling/annotation guidelines is hard. **A good guideline should explain *why* the task is important.** This will motivate annotators to put in the effort it deserves. Whether the task is labeling images, annotating sentiment in text, or rating search relevance, tell them why it matters. **Next, explain the task so annotators understand exactly what they need to do.** This may involve helping annotators put themselves in the shoes of users, and possibly breaking the task into smaller pieces. For the seemingly basic task of rating search relevance, Google’s guidelines includes definitions for “query”, “locale”, and even “results”. To help annotators understand what they’re rating (i.e., search queries), Google includes several examples of queries and their intents. To help annotators decide better and increase precision, we can provide examples of tasks with their associated output and explanations. If Cohen’s kappa stays consistent or increases as you iterate on your task definition and labeling guidelines, you’re on the right track. How to Write Data Labeling/Annotation Guidelines.
